newsitem.title: UK: World Insurance Network gives more price details.
newsitem.headline: World Insurance Network gives more price details.

text.p: The World Insurance Network (WIN) on Monday gave more details about its pricing structure and confirmed that it will go ahead with its launch as planned on July 1.
WIN is an electronic information system being developed by the four top insurance brokers -- J&H Marsh & McLennan, Aon, Sedgwick and Willis Corroon.
The pricing structure for the first stage of its electronic commerce product, WINconnect, breaks down into three areas, WIN said in a statement.
There is a one-off membership fee equivalent to 50 percent of the first year's subscription fee. This has been capped at no more than 50,000 stg and no less than 2,500 stg.
The statement said traffic and connection costs will be published before July 1. A spokesman said this would probably be in June, but was unable to give further details.
WIN's first users will be the founding brokers and the named testing partners Commercial Union, Generali, Gerling, Cigna, Royal & Sun Alliance and XL Insurance.

Subscription fees vary for brokers and carriers. Brokers will pay 15 stg per 100,000 stg of retained brokerage and underwriters/carriers will pay 10 stg per 100,000 stg gross written premium. Both have a maximum of up to 100,000 stg but no lower than 5,000 stg.
After July 1, WINconnect will be available to any broker or carrier who wants to join the network.
WIN is expected to help insurers and brokers cut costs and save time by reducing the amount of data that is rekeyed.

Robert J. Cooney, President of Bermuda-based XL Insurance, said, "Our submissions are massive; they arrive in Bermuda by courier and are then all scanned and re-keyed into our document management and underwriting systems. With WIN, they will be arriving in digital form, thus saving us enormous amounts of time in the management of both documents and data."
